items.prompt:
**Statement:** All the seats in the 9:15 local train to Thane were occupied when it left Dadar station today.

**Conclusions:**
I. No seat was vacant in the 9:15 Thane local when it left Dadar today.
II. The 9:15 Thane local is crowded every day.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: "all seats occupied" means no seat was vacant — it simply restates the statement.
II does not follow: the statement is about today only; "every day" is a generalisation it does not support.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A single observation never supports an "every day" conclusion.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Ramesh scored 82 marks in the Mathematics test, which is 10 marks more than Suresh scored in the same test.

**Conclusions:**
I. Ramesh is better at Mathematics than Suresh in every test.
II. Suresh scored 72 marks in the Mathematics test.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: one test says nothing about "every test".
II follows: 82 − 10 = 72.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Beating someone once does not make you better "in every test".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The bakery on Station Road sold out its plum cakes by noon on Christmas Eve.

**Conclusions:**
I. The bakery had baked too few plum cakes.
II. Plum cakes are the most popular item at the bakery.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: selling out may be due to high demand or a deliberately small batch; "too few" is a judgement the statement does not make.
II does not follow: no other item is compared, so "most popular" is unsupported.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Selling out is a fact; the reason for it and comparisons with other items are outside the statement.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Every employee of Sharma Textiles who completed the safety course this month received a certificate. Anita, an employee of Sharma Textiles, completed the safety course this month.

**Conclusions:**
I. Anita received a certificate.
II. At least one employee of Sharma Textiles has received a certificate.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: Anita is an employee who completed the course this month, so the "every" rule applies to her.
II follows: Anita is such an employee, so at least one employee has received a certificate.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: II looks vague, but "at least one" is guaranteed by Anita herself.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The district collector will announce on Friday whether the schools in the district will stay closed next Monday because of heavy rain.

**Conclusions:**
I. The schools in the district will stay closed next Monday.
II. The schools in the district will not stay closed next Monday.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the decision has not been announced yet.
But I and II have the same subject and are exact opposites; one of them must be true. So they form a complementary pair: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: Choosing "Neither" misses that the two conclusions together cover every possibility.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Meera's flight to Kochi was delayed by three hours because of fog at Delhi airport.

**Conclusions:**
I. There was fog at Delhi airport.
II. All flights from Delhi airport were delayed that day.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the statement gives fog at Delhi airport as the cause of the delay, so there was fog.
II does not follow: only Meera's flight is mentioned; "all flights" is an extreme generalisation.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: "All" in a conclusion needs "all" in the statement.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The price of tomatoes in the city market has doubled in the past two weeks.

**Conclusions:**
I. Tomato farmers are earning double their usual income.
II. People in the city have stopped buying tomatoes.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the retail price says nothing about what farmers receive or how much they sell.
II does not follow: a price rise may reduce buying, but "stopped buying" is an extreme claim the statement does not support.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Market price ≠ farmer income, and a costlier item is not necessarily an item nobody buys.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Of the 40 students in Class 8B, 25 are girls.

**Conclusions:**
I. Girls perform better than boys in Class 8B.
II. There are 15 boys in Class 8B.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: numbers say nothing about performance.
II follows: 40 − 25 = 15 students are boys.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: More girls does not mean better girls.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The library will remain closed on Sunday and Monday for the annual stock check.

**Conclusions:**
I. The library will not be open on Monday.
II. The library carries out a stock check every year.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the library will remain closed on Monday.
II follows: "annual" means yearly, so the stock check is carried out every year.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Some students reject II as "outside information", but it is the plain meaning of "annual" in the statement.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Only members holding a valid card can borrow books from the Riverside Club library.

**Conclusions:**
I. A person without a valid card cannot borrow books from the Riverside Club library.
II. Every member holding a valid card borrows books from the library.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: "only card-holding members can borrow" means nobody without a valid card can borrow.
II does not follow: being allowed to borrow does not mean every card-holder actually borrows.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: "Only X can do Y" does not mean "every X does Y" — that is the converse error.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** With the 120 buses added this year and none withdrawn from service, the State Transport Corporation now has 2,400 buses.

**Conclusions:**
I. The corporation had 2,280 buses at the start of this year.
II. The corporation's buses are now less crowded than before.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: no buses were withdrawn, so the earlier fleet was 2,400 − 120 = 2,280.
II does not follow: the number of passengers is not given; more buses do not by themselves prove less crowding.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: II sounds likely, but "likely" is not enough for a conclusion.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** According to the traffic police, since the new flyover opened, the average peak-hour travel time between Hebbal and the airport has fallen from 70 minutes to 45 minutes.

**Conclusions:**
I. The flyover was built mainly to reduce travel time to the airport.
II. According to the traffic police, peak-hour travel between Hebbal and the airport now takes less time on average than it did before the flyover opened.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the statement reports a result, not the purpose for which the flyover was built.
II follows: 45 minutes is less than 70 minutes, as the traffic police reported.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: An effect that happened is not proof of the purpose behind a project.

items.prompt:

**Conclusions:**
I. Most people in Pune skip breakfast on weekdays.
II. Office-goers in Pune do not have time for breakfast.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the survey covered office-goers only, so the result cannot be extended to all people in Pune.
II does not follow: the reason for skipping breakfast is not given; lack of time is only a guess.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Both conclusions go beyond the survey — one widens the group, the other supplies a cause.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** No vehicle older than fifteen years will be allowed to ply in the city from 1 April. Ravi's car was bought new eighteen years ago.

**Conclusions:**
I. Ravi's car will not be allowed to ply in the city from 1 April.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: Ravi's car is at least eighteen years old, which is older than fifteen.
II follows: a car bought new sixteen years ago is older than fifteen years, so the rule covers it too.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: II is not about Ravi, but it applies the same general rule to another case.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The investigating team has said that the fire at the godown was caused either by an electrical short circuit or by a carelessly thrown cigarette, and that it will name the exact cause after laboratory tests.

**Conclusions:**
I. The fire at the godown was caused by an electrical short circuit.
II. The fire at the godown was caused by a carelessly thrown cigarette.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the exact cause has not been named yet.
But the statement says the cause is one of these two, so exactly one of I and II must be true: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: Picking "Neither" ignores the "either … or" that limits the cause to these two.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** In the inter-school quiz, St. Joseph's finished ahead of Kendriya Vidyalaya, and Kendriya Vidyalaya finished ahead of Modern School.

**Conclusions:**
I. St. Joseph's finished ahead of Modern School.
II. St. Joseph's won the quiz.

solution.trap: Being first among three named schools is not the same as winning the whole quiz.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Mr Kulkarni, a retired bank officer, said that he now walks five kilometres every morning, something he could never find time for while he was working.

**Conclusions:**
I. Mr Kulkarni was unfit while he worked at the bank.
II. Mr Kulkarni did not walk five kilometres every morning while he was working.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: not walking does not mean he was unfit; nothing is said about his health.
II follows: he says he could never find time for it while working.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Missing one form of exercise tells us nothing about overall fitness.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The number of passengers using the city's metro rose by 18 per cent in the month after fares were cut by 10 per cent.

**Conclusions:**
I. The fare cut was the reason for the rise in the number of metro passengers.
II. The metro will cut its fares further next year.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the rise came after the cut, but the statement does not say it was caused by it (festivals, new lines or road works could also be responsible).
II does not follow: nothing is said about future fare decisions.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Sequence in time is not proof of cause.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Under a new rule, a bank customer who fails to update the KYC details by 31 March will not be able to withdraw money from the account until the details are updated. Farah, a customer of the bank, had not updated her KYC details by 31 March.

**Conclusions:**
I. Farah cannot withdraw money from her account until she updates her KYC details.
II. At least one customer of the bank will be unable to withdraw money from their account for some time after 31 March.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: Farah is exactly the kind of customer the rule covers.
II follows: Farah herself is such a customer, so at least one customer is affected.

solution.trap: II seems too general to judge, but Farah is a guaranteed example.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Neha is taller than Arjun but shorter than Kabir. Kabir is shorter than Dev.

**Conclusions:**
I. Dev is taller than Neha.
II. Neha is the second tallest of the four.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Order from tallest: Dev > Kabir > Neha > Arjun. I follows: Dev is taller than Neha.
II does not follow: Neha is the third tallest, not the second.

solution.trap: Write the full order before judging — Neha sits below both Kabir and Dev.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The railway board has announced that, from next month, passengers will for the first time be able to book tickets for unreserved coaches through its mobile app.

**Conclusions:**
I. Most passengers will book their unreserved tickets through the app from next month.
II. At present, passengers cannot book tickets for unreserved coaches through the railway's mobile app.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the facility will exist, but how many passengers will use it is only a prediction.
II follows: "for the first time" from next month means the facility is not available now.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Availability of a facility does not tell you how many will use it.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A leading cardiologist said at a seminar that people who climb stairs daily have a lower risk of heart disease than those who do not.

**Conclusions:**
I. Climbing stairs daily will prevent heart disease.
II. People who do not climb stairs daily will develop heart disease.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: a lower risk is not prevention; "will prevent" is far stronger than the statement.

Answer: Neither I nor II follows.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The company's annual report shows that its profit rose from ₹40 crore last year to ₹50 crore this year, even though its sales remained unchanged.

**Conclusions:**

II. The company earned more profit on the same sales this year than last year.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the rise is ₹10 crore on ₹40 crore, i.e. 25 per cent.
II follows: sales were unchanged while profit went up.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Check the base: 10 on 40 is 25 per cent, not 20 per cent.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Mohan has been told that after his training he will be posted either to the Nagpur branch or to the Nashik branch, and to no other place.

**Conclusions:**
I. Mohan will be posted to the Nagpur branch after his training.
II. Mohan will be posted to the Nashik branch after his training.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: which of the two branches it will be is not stated.
But the posting is limited to exactly these two branches, so one of I and II must be true: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: The phrase "and to no other place" is what makes the pair complementary.

items.prompt:

solution.trap: II needs outside knowledge about solar power, which a conclusion may not use.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Heavy rain for three days has flooded several low-lying areas of Guwahati, and the district administration has opened relief camps in 12 of the city's schools.

**Conclusions:**
I. All schools in Guwahati have been shut.

Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: "Some" is supported by the 12 schools; "all" is not.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Sunita has cleared the preliminary examination for the post of probationary officer.

**Conclusions:**
I. Sunita will be appointed as a probationary officer.
II. Sunita is well prepared for the main examination.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: clearing the preliminary stage does not guarantee selection; later stages remain.

Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Passing one stage is not a guarantee of the final result.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A notice at the city museum reads: 'Photography is permitted in all galleries except the Manuscripts Gallery, where flash may damage the exhibits.'

**Conclusions:**
I. If the museum has a Textiles Gallery, photography is permitted in it.
II. Photography without flash is permitted in the Manuscripts Gallery.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: photography is allowed in every gallery except one, so any other gallery, including a Textiles Gallery, allows it.
II does not follow: the notice bars all photography in the Manuscripts Gallery; flash is only the reason given, not the limit of the ban.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A reason for a rule does not narrow the rule itself.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Of the 200 applicants for the clerk post, 150 knew typing and 120 knew Hindi. Every applicant knew at least one of the two.

**Conclusions:**
I. Every applicant who knew Hindi also knew typing.
II. At least 70 applicants knew both typing and Hindi.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Both = 150 + 120 − 200 = 70. So 120 − 70 = 50 applicants knew Hindi but not typing; I does not follow.
II follows: exactly 70 applicants knew both, which satisfies "at least 70".
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: The overlap is forced by "every applicant knew at least one".

items.prompt:

**Conclusions:**

II. A property owner who pays the full tax in November will pay more than the tax amount.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 15 June is before 30 June, so the 5 per cent rebate applies.
II follows: November is after 30 September, so a penalty is added.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Check each date against the correct window; both fall inside a stated rule.

items.prompt:

**Conclusions:**
I. Buying a two-wheeler makes a household spend more on groceries.
II. Every household in the study that owned a two-wheeler spent more on groceries than every household that did not.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the study shows an association, not a cause; income could explain both.
II does not follow: a higher average does not mean every member of one group exceeds every member of the other.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: An average comparison is not an "every" comparison, and association is not causation.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The bank's new policy states that any loan application above ₹10 lakh must be approved by the regional manager, in addition to the branch manager.

**Conclusions:**

II. The regional manager does not deal with loan applications of ₹10 lakh or less.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: ₹15 lakh is above ₹10 lakh, so the regional manager's approval is also needed.
II does not follow: the policy says when the regional manager must approve; it does not bar the regional manager from other applications.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: "Must approve above X" does not mean "never deals with below X".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Mr Rao said, 'I have been living in this town for twenty years, and in all that time the river has flooded the market only twice.'

**Conclusions:**
I. Floods in the market are rare because the river is well managed.
II. According to Mr Rao, there have been years in the last twenty in which the river did not flood the market.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: no reason for the low number of floods is given.
II follows: two floods in twenty years leaves at least eighteen years without a flood.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: I adds a cause the statement never mentions.

**Conclusions:**
I. The two banks will sign a merger agreement this week.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the outcome is not yet known.
The statement says the talks will end in exactly one of these two ways this week, so I and II are complementary: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: The "either … or" in the statement is what makes the pair complementary.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Following complaints about noise, the housing board has banned the use of loudspeakers in residential areas after 10 p.m.

**Conclusions:**
I. All the complaints about noise were about loudspeakers.
II. Loudspeakers may be used in residential areas before 10 p.m. without any restriction.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the complaints were about noise; nothing says every complaint concerned loudspeakers.
II does not follow: the ban covers only the hours after 10 p.m.; it says nothing about whether other rules limit use earlier. "Without any restriction" goes too far.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Silence about earlier hours is not permission "without any restriction".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Every candidate who scored above 60 in the written test was called for the interview, and no candidate who scored 60 or below was called. Rakesh was called for the interview; Imran scored 58.

**Conclusions:**
I. Rakesh scored above 60 in the written test.
II. Imran was not called for the interview.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: nobody with 60 or below was called, so Rakesh, who was called, must have scored above 60.
II follows: 58 is below 60, and no such candidate was called.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: The second rule ("no one with 60 or below") is what lets you reason backwards for Rakesh.

items.prompt:

**Conclusions:**
I. On a weekday, films are screened in at most one of the town's cinema halls.
II. Cinema halls in the town are closing because people prefer to watch films at home.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: only two halls are left and one of them is closed on weekdays, so at most one can screen films on a weekday.
II does not follow: no reason for the closures is given.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: "At most one" is safe even if the other hall happens to be shut on some weekday.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The weather office has forecast that the monsoon will reach Kerala on 4 June, three days later than its normal date of onset.

**Conclusions:**
I. The monsoon will be weak this year.
II. The normal date of the monsoon's onset over Kerala is 1 June.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: a late start says nothing about how strong the monsoon will be.
II follows: three days before 4 June is 1 June.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Timing and strength are different things.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Anil told his friend that he would join the gym only if it opened a branch within two kilometres of his house.

**Conclusions:**
I. Anil will join the gym if it opens a branch within two kilometres of his house.
II. Anil cannot afford to travel more than two kilometres to a gym.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: "only if" gives a necessary condition, not a sufficient one; a nearby branch does not guarantee he will join.
II does not follow: the reason for his condition (cost, time, habit) is not stated.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Reading "only if" as "if" is the commonest error in these questions.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** In the class test, every student who scored full marks in Part A also scored full marks in Part B. Priya did not score full marks in Part B. Gopal scored full marks in Part A.

**Conclusions:**
I. Priya did not score full marks in Part A.
II. Gopal scored full marks in Part B.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: if Priya had full marks in Part A she would have full marks in Part B, which she does not (contrapositive).
II follows: Gopal had full marks in Part A, so by the rule he had full marks in Part B.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: The contrapositive is valid; only the converse is not.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: The State Electricity Board said that power cuts in rural areas this summer averaged four hours a day, down from six hours a day last summer. It attributed the improvement to a new 500-megawatt plant commissioned in January, but added that demand is expected to grow by 8 per cent next year.

**Conclusions:**
I. The new plant is the only reason power cuts in rural areas came down this summer.
II. On average, rural consumers had more hours of power supply per day this summer than last summer.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the board credits the plant, but nothing says it was the only reason; "only" is an extreme word.
II follows: average cuts fell from six to four hours a day, so average supply rose from 18 to 20 hours a day.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Attributing a result to one cause is not saying it is the sole cause.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: A survey by a consumer forum found that 70 per cent of online shoppers in metro cities returned at least one product in the past year, most often citing wrong size. The forum has asked e-commerce firms to put detailed size charts on every product page.

**Conclusions:**
I. Most online shoppers in India return the products they buy.
II. Detailed size charts will bring the share of shoppers who return products below 70 per cent.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the survey covers metro cities only, and "returned at least one product" is not "return the products they buy".
II does not follow: the forum hopes size charts will help, but whether they will reduce returns is a prediction, not a conclusion.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: I widens both the group and the behaviour; II treats a suggestion as a certain outcome.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: The civic body has made rainwater harvesting compulsory for all new buildings on plots above 300 square metres. Buildings approved before 1 January 2026 are exempt, while the owners of new buildings that do not comply will pay a penalty of 5 per cent of the property tax every year until they do.

**Conclusions:**
I. The owner of a new building on a 500-square-metre plot, approved in March 2026, who has not installed rainwater harvesting will have to pay a penalty.
II. Buildings on plots of 300 square metres or less do not need to harvest rainwater.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the plot is above 300 square metres, approval in March 2026 is after the exemption date, and the owner has not complied.
II does not follow: the rule is silent on smaller plots; silence does not mean they are free of every such requirement (another rule could apply).
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A rule that covers X says nothing about what applies to non-X.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: Sales of electric scooters in the state rose from 20,000 in 2024 to 50,000 in 2025, while sales of petrol scooters fell from 3,00,000 to 2,70,000 over the same period.

**Conclusions:**

II. Electric scooters made up a larger share of the combined sales of electric and petrol scooters in 2025 than in 2024.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Do the arithmetic before assuming the totals must have changed.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: Talks between the transporters' union and the state government ended without agreement on Monday. The union has said that its members will either resume work on Thursday or begin an indefinite strike from that day, depending on whether the government accepts its demand for a toll waiver by Wednesday night.

**Conclusions:**
I. The transporters' union will begin an indefinite strike from Thursday.
II. Members of the transporters' union will resume work on Thursday.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the outcome depends on a government decision not yet taken.
The statement says exactly one of the two will happen on Thursday, so I and II are complementary: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: The failed talks tempt you towards I, but the government can still accept the demand.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: A report by the state health department says that dengue cases in the city fell from 4,200 in 2024 to 2,900 in 2025. The department credited its fogging drive, but independent experts pointed out that the city also received 30 per cent less rainfall in 2025.

**Conclusions:**
I. The fogging drive did not contribute to the fall in dengue cases.
II. The report attributes the fall in dengue cases at least partly to the department's fogging drive.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the experts only point to another possible factor; they do not show the fogging had no effect.
II follows: the department "credited its fogging drive" for the fall.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: An alternative explanation weakens a claim; it does not disprove it.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: The central bank kept its policy rate unchanged at 6.5 per cent for the fifth meeting in a row, saying that inflation, though easing, remained above its target of 4 per cent.

**Conclusions:**
I. The central bank will cut its policy rate at its next meeting.
II. Inflation is now higher than it was at the central bank's previous meeting.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: easing inflation may make a cut more likely, but the next decision is not stated.
II does not follow: inflation is described as "easing", i.e. falling, even though it is still above the 4 per cent target.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: "Above target" is about the level; "easing" is about the direction — do not mix them up.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: The university announced that from this academic year, students who fail in not more than two papers of a semester will be promoted to the next semester, but must clear those papers within the following two semesters. Students failing in three or more papers will have to repeat the semester.

**Conclusions:**
I. A student who fails in exactly two papers of a semester this academic year will not have to repeat that semester.
II. Before this academic year, a student who failed in two papers had to repeat the semester.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: two papers is "not more than two", so the student is promoted rather than made to repeat.
II does not follow: "from this academic year" suggests a change, but the old rule is not stated — it may have been stricter in some other way.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: Knowing a rule is new does not tell you what the old rule was.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: In the city's municipal school system, 1,200 of the 1,500 sanctioned teaching posts are filled. The education committee has decided to fill all the vacant posts before the next academic session, and has said that at least half of the new appointments will be of science teachers.

**Conclusions:**
I. At present, 300 teaching posts in the city's municipal schools are vacant.
II. If the committee's decision is carried out as stated, at least 150 science teachers will be appointed.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 1,500 − 1,200 = 300 posts are vacant.
II follows: filling all 300 vacancies with at least half going to science teachers means at least 150 science teachers.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: II is conditional ("if carried out"), so it is a definite consequence, not a prediction.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** News item: A private airline said its on-time performance improved to 88 per cent in August from 81 per cent in July, the best among domestic carriers for August. The airline added two new aircraft to its fleet in August.

**Conclusions:**
I. The two new aircraft helped the airline improve its on-time performance.
II. In August, no other domestic carrier had an on-time performance above 88 per cent.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the two facts are placed side by side, but no link between the new aircraft and punctuality is stated.
II follows: 88 per cent was the best among domestic carriers in August, so no other carrier was above it.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Two facts in the same report are not cause and effect.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The Andheri branch of a bank will remain closed on Saturday, 14 November, as its office is being shifted to a new building on the same road.

**Conclusions:**
I. The Andheri branch of the bank will not be open for business on 14 November.
II. The new building has more space than the branch's present office.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: a branch that will "remain closed" on 14 November will not be open for business that day.
II does not follow: the statement gives no comparison of the two buildings; a move may be made for many reasons.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A shift of premises tells you nothing about the size of the new premises.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A mobile recharge plan costs ₹299 and gives 2 GB of data a day for 28 days.

**Conclusions:**
I. The ₹299 plan is the cheapest plan offered by the company.
II. The ₹299 plan gives 56 GB of data in all over its 28 days.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: no other plan of the company is mentioned, so "cheapest" cannot be judged.
II follows: 2 GB a day for 28 days is 2 × 28 = 56 GB.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: A single price can never establish "cheapest" without the other prices.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The district education office will put the result of last month's scholarship test on its website next week. Gaurav took the test.

**Conclusions:**
I. Gaurav's name will appear in the list of candidates who qualified in the scholarship test.
II. Gaurav's name will not appear in the list of candidates who qualified in the scholarship test.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the result has not been published, so we do not know how Gaurav did.
But Gaurav took the test and the result will be published, so his name will either be in the qualified list or not. I and II are exact opposites about the same person: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: "Result not yet known" tempts you to pick "Neither", but the two conclusions together cover every case.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The new shopping mall on Kanpur Road in Lucknow drew 50,000 visitors on its opening day.

**Conclusions:**
I. The mall will draw about 50,000 visitors every day.
II. The mall has more shops than any other mall in Lucknow.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: opening-day crowds are a one-day figure and say nothing about daily visitors later.
II does not follow: the number of shops is not mentioned, and no other mall is compared.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: An opening-day figure is not a daily average.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** All the trains on the Chennai–Bengaluru route have been fitted with bio-toilets. The Lalbagh Express runs on the Chennai–Bengaluru route.

**Conclusions:**
I. The Lalbagh Express has been fitted with bio-toilets.
II. No train without bio-toilets runs on the Chennai–Bengaluru route.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the Lalbagh Express is one of the trains on the route, and all of them have bio-toilets.
II follows: if every train on the route has bio-toilets, a train without them cannot be one of the trains on the route.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: II is just the first sentence turned round correctly (contrapositive); it is not the converse error.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The canteen of Sardar Patel Vidyalaya has stopped selling packaged soft drinks from this week.

**Conclusions:**
I. Packaged soft drinks cannot be bought at the school's canteen this week.
II. Students of the school no longer drink packaged soft drinks.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the canteen has stopped selling them from this week.
II does not follow: students may still buy soft drinks elsewhere; the statement is only about the canteen.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A rule about one shop says nothing about what students do outside it.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Kavya reached the examination centre at 9:40 a.m., twenty minutes before its gate closed.

**Conclusions:**
I. Kavya always reaches places well before time.
II. The gate of the examination centre closed at 10:00 a.m.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: one early arrival does not show what Kavya "always" does.
II follows: twenty minutes after 9:40 a.m. is 10:00 a.m.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: "Always" needs evidence about many occasions, not one.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The final of the inter-school cricket tournament between Green Valley School and Sunrise School will be played on Saturday. The tournament rules say the final must produce a winner.

**Conclusions:**
I. Green Valley School will win the final.
II. Sunrise School will win the final.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the match has not been played yet.
But only these two schools play the final, and the rules say it must produce a winner, so exactly one of I and II will be true: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: "Must produce a winner" rules out a draw, which is what makes the pair complementary.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Doctors at the district hospital have advised people to drink only boiled water during the monsoon.

**Conclusions:**
I. Drinking water that has not been boiled during the monsoon will make people ill.
II. Everyone in the district drinks boiled water during the monsoon.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: advice points to a risk, but "will make people ill" is a certainty the statement does not give.
II does not follow: the doctors have given advice; whether everyone follows it is not stated.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Advice about what people should do is not a report of what they do, and a risk is not a certainty.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Water supply to Sectors 4 and 5 will be suspended from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Tuesday for repair work on the main pipeline.

**Conclusions:**
I. Residents of Sector 5 will not get piped water supply at noon on Tuesday.
II. Water supply to Sector 4 will be suspended for six hours on Tuesday.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: noon falls between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., when supply to Sector 5 is suspended.
II follows: 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. is six hours.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Both are read straight off the notice; there is no hidden catch.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A bank has announced that, from April, savings accounts with an average monthly balance below ₹5,000 will be charged ₹50 for that month.

**Conclusions:**
I. A savings account of the bank with an average balance of ₹4,000 in May will be charged ₹50 for May.
II. Most of the bank's customers keep an average balance below ₹5,000.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: May is after the rule starts and ₹4,000 is below ₹5,000, so the ₹50 charge applies.
II does not follow: the statement gives the rule, not how many customers fall below the limit.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A charge aimed at low balances does not mean most customers have low balances.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Ankit, a clerk at a cooperative bank, has been promoted to assistant manager after clearing the internal promotion test in his first attempt.

**Conclusions:**
I. Ankit was the best clerk in his branch.
II. Ankit cleared the internal promotion test without needing a second attempt.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: no other clerk is compared with Ankit; clearing a test does not make him the best.
II follows: he cleared the test in his first attempt, so no second attempt was needed.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Promotion is not a ranking against colleagues.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The selection committee will meet on Friday to name the captain of the state under-19 cricket team. It has said the captain will be either Rohan or Vikram.

**Conclusions:**
I. Rohan will be named captain of the state under-19 team.
II. Vikram will be named captain of the state under-19 team.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the committee has not yet decided between them.
But the captain will be one of exactly these two, and a team has one captain, so one of I and II must be true: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: Choosing "Neither" ignores that the choice is limited to these two players.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A bank has reduced the interest rate on its one-year fixed deposits from 7 per cent to 6.5 per cent.

**Conclusions:**
I. Customers will stop opening one-year fixed deposits with the bank.
II. The bank has reduced the interest rates on all its deposits.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: a lower rate may reduce interest, but "stop opening" is an extreme prediction.
II does not follow: only the one-year fixed deposit rate is mentioned; other deposits may be unchanged.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: A cut on one product is not a cut on all products.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A bank charges a fee of ₹20 for every cash withdrawal from other banks' ATMs beyond the first five in a month. In July, Nidhi, a customer of the bank, made seven cash withdrawals from other banks' ATMs.

**Conclusions:**
I. Nidhi will be charged ₹40 under this rule for her July withdrawals.
II. Five of Nidhi's July withdrawals from other banks' ATMs will not attract this fee.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: seven withdrawals is two beyond five, and 2 × ₹20 = ₹40.
II follows: the first five withdrawals in the month are outside the fee.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Count only the withdrawals beyond five: 7 − 5 = 2, not 7.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Under a new rule, a student must have at least 75 per cent attendance in Class 11 to be allowed to sit the Class 11 final examination. Sheetal's attendance in Class 11 is 70 per cent.

**Conclusions:**
I. Sheetal will not be allowed to sit the Class 11 final examination.
II. Every student with at least 75 per cent attendance will pass the Class 11 final examination.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 75 per cent attendance is required to sit the examination, and Sheetal has only 70 per cent.
II does not follow: attendance only decides who may sit the examination, not who passes it.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A condition for sitting an examination is not a guarantee of passing it.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The pollution control board has ordered all stone-crushing units within 5 km of the city limits to shut down for 15 days because of severe air pollution.

**Conclusions:**
I. Stone-crushing units are the main cause of air pollution in the city.
II. A stone-crushing unit located 3 km from the city limits must shut down for 15 days.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the units have been shut because of pollution, but nothing says they are the main source of it.
II follows: 3 km is within 5 km, so the order covers this unit.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Being one target of an order does not make something the main cause.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The Kolkata branch of a bank opened at least as many new savings accounts in September as its Howrah branch did.

**Conclusions:**
I. The Kolkata branch opened more new savings accounts in September than the Howrah branch.
II. The Kolkata and Howrah branches opened the same number of new savings accounts in September.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: "At least as many" means Kolkata ≥ Howrah. Neither I (Kolkata > Howrah) nor II (Kolkata = Howrah) is certain on its own.
But ≥ is made up of exactly these two cases, so one of them must be true: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: "At least as many" splits into "more than" or "equal to" — a classic complementary pair.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The state government has launched a scheme to give free LED bulbs to households in rural areas.

**Conclusions:**
I. All rural households in the state now use LED bulbs.
II. The scheme will reduce the electricity bills of rural households.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: a scheme being launched does not mean every household has received or uses the bulbs; "all" is extreme.
II does not follow: the effect on bills is not stated; it would need outside knowledge and assumptions about use.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: The launch of a scheme is not proof of its reach or its results.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Every member of the Green Lake Residents' Association paid this year's annual fee of ₹1,200. The association has 150 members.

**Conclusions:**
I. The association received ₹1,80,000 from its members as this year's annual fee.
II. No member of the association failed to pay this year's annual fee.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 150 members × ₹1,200 = ₹1,80,000.
II follows: every member paid, so none failed to pay.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: II is a double negative of "every member paid"; read it slowly.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The forest department's census counted 120 leopards in the Bhadra sanctuary this year, against 96 four years ago.

**Conclusions:**
I. The number of leopards counted in the sanctuary has risen by 25 per cent in four years.
II. The Bhadra sanctuary has more leopards than any other sanctuary in the state.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the rise is 24 on a base of 96, and 24 ÷ 96 = 25 per cent.
II does not follow: no other sanctuary is mentioned.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: Take the old figure (96) as the base, not the new one; 24 on 120 would give 20 per cent.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A survey by the telecom regulator found that the average 4G download speed in the state rose from 12 Mbps to 18 Mbps during the year.

**Conclusions:**
I. Every 4G user in the state got faster download speeds by the end of the year.
II. The average 4G download speed in the state rose by 50 per cent during the year.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: a higher average can hide some users whose speed stayed the same or fell.
II follows: the rise is 6 Mbps on 12 Mbps, i.e. 50 per cent.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: A rise in the average is not a rise for every user.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The answer key for a class test says the correct answer to Question 17 is either (b) or (d); a correction notice will state which. Meena marked (b) for Question 17.

**Conclusions:**
I. Meena's answer to Question 17 is correct.
II. Meena's answer to Question 17 is wrong.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: we do not yet know whether the correct answer is (b) or (d).
But Meena's answer is either right or wrong — if the key is (b) she is right, if (d) she is wrong. I and II are exact opposites: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: Not knowing which outcome has happened is not the same as neither outcome happening.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Twelve students of a government higher secondary school in Erode have qualified for the state-level science olympiad this year, the highest number from any school in Erode district.

**Conclusions:**
I. The school has the best science teachers in Erode district.
II. No school in the state had more students qualify for the olympiad this year.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the result may have many causes; the quality of teachers is not mentioned.
II does not follow: the school leads only within Erode district, not the whole state.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: "Highest in the district" is not "highest in the state".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** From 1 January, shops and commercial establishments in the state's cities will be allowed to stay open 24 hours a day, provided they give every worker one weekly holiday.

**Conclusions:**
I. After 1 January, a city shop that does not give every worker a weekly holiday will not get this permission to stay open 24 hours a day.
II. After 1 January, a city shop that gives every worker a weekly holiday may stay open through the night.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the permission is given "provided" every worker gets a weekly holiday, so a shop that does not meet this condition does not get it.
II follows: a shop meeting the condition is allowed to stay open 24 hours, which includes the night.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: "Allowed … provided" makes the weekly holiday a condition of the permission.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** From 1 December, the municipal corporation will issue birth and death certificates only in digital form through its online portal.

**Conclusions:**
I. After 1 December, the corporation will not issue birth certificates on paper.
II. All residents of the city can use the corporation's online portal.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: "only in digital form" rules out paper certificates being issued by the corporation.
II does not follow: the statement says how certificates will be issued, not that every resident is able to use the portal.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: II is something the corporation may be hoping for; it is not stated or implied as a fact.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A garment exporter in Tiruppur employs 600 workers at its only factory. It has decided to open a second factory that will employ 400 workers.

**Conclusions:**
I. The exporter's export orders have increased.
II. If the second factory starts with its planned workforce and the first factory keeps all its 600 workers, the exporter will employ 1,000 workers in all.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the reason for the new factory is not given; more orders is only one possible reason.
II follows: under the stated condition, 600 + 400 = 1,000 workers.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: A business decision does not reveal its reason unless the statement gives it.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The bank has told Mr Sethi that his home-loan application will be either approved or rejected within seven working days, and will not be kept pending beyond that.

**Conclusions:**
I. Mr Sethi's home-loan application will be approved within seven working days.
II. Mr Sethi's home-loan application will be rejected within seven working days.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither I nor II follows on its own: the bank has not yet decided.
But the bank has said the application will end in exactly one of these two ways within seven working days: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: "Will not be kept pending" closes the third possibility, so the pair is complementary.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A study of 2,000 adults in Chennai found that those who slept less than six hours a night were more likely to be overweight than those who slept longer.

**Conclusions:**
I. Sleeping less than six hours a night makes people overweight.
II. Most adults in Chennai sleep less than six hours a night.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the study shows a link, not a cause; stress or eating habits could explain both short sleep and weight.
II does not follow: the study does not say how many adults slept less than six hours.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: "More likely to be" describes an association, not a cause.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** In a school of 900 students, the ratio of boys to girls is 4 : 5.

**Conclusions:**
I. There are 100 more girls than boys in the school.
II. Girls make up more than half of the school's students.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 500 − 400 = 100. II follows: 500 out of 900 is more than half.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Divide 900 by 9 (4 + 5), not by 4 or 5.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Of the 80 streetlights on MG Road, 18 were found not working during the ward officer's inspection last night; the rest were working.

**Conclusions:**
I. More than three-fourths of the streetlights on MG Road were working during the inspection.
II. The streetlights on MG Road failed because of poor maintenance.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 80 − 18 = 62 lights were working, and 62 is more than 60 (three-fourths of 80).
II does not follow: no reason for the faults is given.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: Compare with three-fourths of 80 = 60, not with 18.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The traffic police have announced a fine of ₹500 for parking on the footpaths of the newly paved Ring Road.

**Conclusions:**
I. Parking on footpaths in other parts of the city is allowed.
II. A motorist found parked on a footpath of the Ring Road can be fined ₹500.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the announcement is about the Ring Road only; it says nothing about footpaths elsewhere, and silence is not permission.
II follows: this is exactly what the announced fine covers.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: A rule for one road does not make the opposite true for all other roads.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Rice production in Bardhaman district this year was not lower than last year's.

**Conclusions:**
I. Rice production in Bardhaman district rose this year.
II. Rice production in Bardhaman district this year was the same as last year's.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: "Not lower" means this year ≥ last year. Neither a rise (I) nor an equal figure (II) is certain on its own.
These two cases together make up "not lower", so one of them must be true: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: "Not lower" does not mean "higher" — it leaves room for "equal".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A popular restaurant chain in Hyderabad has started home delivery of meals in three new localities.

**Conclusions:**
I. Sales at the chain's restaurants have fallen.
II. Home delivery earns the chain more profit than meals served at its restaurants.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the reason for starting delivery is not given; falling sales is only a guess.
II does not follow: no profit figures for either kind of business are given.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Supplying a motive or a comparison the statement never gives is the commonest error here.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The city's air-quality index was in the 'severe' category on every day of the first week of November.

**Conclusions:**
I. The city's air-quality index was in the 'severe' category on 5 November.
II. The city's air-quality index stayed in the 'severe' category for seven days in a row.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 5 November falls in the first week of November.
II follows: the first week of November (1 to 7 November) is seven consecutive days, and the index was severe on each of them.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: "Every day of the first week" covers both a single date in it and the whole run of seven days.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A biscuit company has reduced the weight of its ₹10 pack from 100 grams to 80 grams without changing the price.

**Conclusions:**
I. Buyers of the ₹10 pack now pay more per gram of biscuits than before.
II. The company made this change because its costs had gone up.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: ₹10 for 80 grams (12.5 paise a gram) is more than ₹10 for 100 grams (10 paise a gram).
II does not follow: the reason for the change is not stated.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: Same price, less quantity means a higher price per unit; the cause is a separate question.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** In this year's Class 10 board examination, 88 per cent of the 50,000 students from the district's government schools who took the examination passed.

**Conclusions:**
I. More students from the district's government schools passed this year than last year.
II. 6,000 students from the district's government schools who took the examination did not pass.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: last year's figures are not given.
II follows: 12 per cent did not pass, and 12 per cent of 50,000 is 6,000.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: A high pass rate this year tells you nothing about last year.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Every Class 9 student at Vidya Niketan School, Bengaluru, must take exactly one of Kannada and French as the third language. Tanvi has just joined Class 9 at the school.

**Conclusions:**

But she must take exactly one of the two, so one of I and II will be true and the other false: either I or II follows.

solution.trap: "Exactly one of" is what makes the two conclusions complementary.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** An IT company in Noida has asked its employees to work from the office at least three days a week from next month.

**Conclusions:**

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the reason for the rule is not given, and no comparison of output is made.

solution.trap: "At least three days in the office" is not "every day in the office".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The Kanpur depot of the state transport corporation runs 60 buses, of which 40 are air-conditioned. All its air-conditioned buses run on CNG.

**Conclusions:**
I. At least 40 of the depot's buses run on CNG.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the 40 air-conditioned buses all run on CNG; the other 20 may or may not, so the total is at least 40.
II follows: 60 − 40 = 20 buses are not air-conditioned.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: "At least 40" is safe even though we do not know about the non-AC buses.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Under a state scheme, every girl student who passes Class 12 from a government school this year will receive a bicycle. Meenu, a girl student, passed Class 12 from a government school this year.

**Conclusions:**
I. Meenu will receive a bicycle under the scheme.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

solution.trap: A scheme for one group says nothing about what other groups get elsewhere.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The state health department has made it compulsory for every private hospital with more than 50 beds to have a working fire-safety system by 31 March.

**Conclusions:**

solution.trap: A rule that covers big hospitals does not exempt small ones from everything else.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The metro rail corporation has said that the new Airport Line will open in March or, if safety checks are delayed, in April. It will not open before March or after April.

**Conclusions:**

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

But the line will open in exactly one of these two months, so either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: The last sentence closes every other month, which makes the pair complementary.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The number of migratory birds that visited Chilika Lake this winter was 10 per cent lower than last winter.

**Conclusions:**
I. The lake has become more polluted since last winter.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: no reason for the fall is given; weather or conditions elsewhere could be responsible.

Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: A fall in numbers is not evidence of a particular cause, nor of a continuing trend.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** No candidate who reaches the examination hall after 9:30 a.m. will be allowed to write the bank's recruitment examination. Sameer, a candidate, was allowed to write it.

**Conclusions:**
I. Sameer reached the examination hall by 9:30 a.m.
II. A candidate who reaches the examination hall at 9:45 a.m. will not be allowed to write the examination.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: had Sameer arrived after 9:30 a.m. he would not have been allowed in; he was allowed, so he arrived by 9:30 a.m.
II follows: 9:45 a.m. is after 9:30 a.m., so the rule applies.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Reasoning back from "was allowed" to "arrived in time" is the valid contrapositive, not a guess.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** At a health camp in Nashik district, 1,200 adults were screened for diabetes and 180 of them tested positive.

**Conclusions:**
I. 15 per cent of the adults screened at the camp tested positive for diabetes.
II. 15 per cent of the adults in Nashik district have diabetes.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 180 ÷ 1,200 = 15 per cent.
II does not follow: the people who came to one camp may not be a fair sample of the whole district.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: A rate found in a camp cannot be stretched to the whole district.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Notice in a housing society: 'The swimming pool will remain closed every Monday for cleaning. On all other days it will be open from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.'

**Conclusions:**
I. The swimming pool is cleaned only on Mondays.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the notice says the pool closes on Mondays for cleaning, not that it is never cleaned on other days.
II follows: the pool remains closed all day on Mondays.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: "Closed on Monday for cleaning" does not mean "cleaned only on Monday".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Residents of a colony in Bhopal have complained to the municipal corporation that garbage has not been collected from their area for a week.

**Conclusions:**
I. The municipal corporation has stopped collecting garbage in the whole of Bhopal.
II. The corporation's garbage collectors are on strike.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the complaint is about one colony only.
