Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: One colony's problem is neither a city-wide fact nor proof of a particular cause.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The bank's annual general meeting, held every year in August, has been postponed to October this year because of floods in the city.

**Conclusions:**
I. The bank's annual general meeting will not be held in August this year.
II. The bank's annual general meeting is normally held in August.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: it has been postponed from August to October.
II follows: the statement says the meeting is held every year in August.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Both facts are in the statement; do not reject II as "general knowledge".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Rahul has booked a cab to reach the airport at 6 a.m. for his 8 a.m. flight to Delhi.

**Conclusions:**
I. Rahul will reach Delhi by 10 a.m.
II. Rahul does not own a car.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the flight time is not given, and delays are possible.
II does not follow: people who own cars also book cabs, for example to avoid airport parking.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Booking a cab does not tell you what a person owns.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A bank will not honour a cheque unless it is presented within three months of the date written on it. Arvind's cheque is dated 10 January and was presented on 25 April.

**Conclusions:**
I. The bank will not honour Arvind's cheque.
II. Any cheque presented within three months of its date will be honoured by the bank.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: three months from 10 January ends on 10 April; the cheque was presented on 25 April, so the necessary condition is not met.

II does not follow: "not … unless" makes timely presentation a necessary condition, not a sufficient one; a cheque may still be refused for other reasons, such as a wrong signature or insufficient funds.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: "Not unless X" means "only if X" — X is needed, but X alone does not guarantee the result.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A phone maker's share of smartphone sales in India fell from 20 per cent last year to 16 per cent this year, while the total number of smartphones sold in India rose by 25 per cent.

**Conclusions:**
I. The company sold fewer smartphones in India this year than last year.
II. The company's share of smartphone sales in India fell by 4 percentage points.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Let last year's total be 100: the company sold 20. This year's total is 125, and 16 per cent of 125 is 20. So its sales were unchanged and I does not follow.
II follows: 20 per cent to 16 per cent is a fall of 4 percentage points.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: A falling share in a growing market need not mean falling sales — here the two effects cancel exactly.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The ₹50-lakh cost of a new bridge was shared between the state government and the Centre: the state paid at least half, and the Centre paid the rest.

**Conclusions:**
I. The state government paid more towards the bridge than the Centre.
II. The state government and the Centre paid equal amounts towards the bridge.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: The state paid at least ₹25 lakh, so the Centre paid at most ₹25 lakh: state ≥ Centre.
Neither "more" (I) nor "equal" (II) is certain on its own, but ≥ is made up of exactly these two cases: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: "At least half" includes exactly half, so "more" alone cannot be concluded.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** In a class test marked out of 50, Manav scored more than Neel, and Om scored less than Manav.

**Conclusions:**
I. Om scored more than Neel.
II. Om scored less than Neel.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: We know Manav > Neel and Manav > Om, but nothing links Om and Neel, so neither I nor II follows on its own.
They are not complementary either: Om and Neel could have scored the same marks, in which case both I and II are false. So neither follows.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: Two opposite-looking conclusions form an "either" pair only if they cover every case; here "equal marks" is left out.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A district's literacy rate, the share of its population that can read and write, rose from 60 per cent to 66 per cent between two surveys. The district's population was 20 lakh at both surveys.

**Conclusions:**
I. The number of literate people in the district rose by 1.2 lakh between the two surveys.
II. The number of literate people in the district rose by 10 per cent between the two surveys.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Literate people rose from 60% of 20 lakh = 12 lakh to 66% of 20 lakh = 13.2 lakh.
I follows: the rise is 1.2 lakh. II follows: 1.2 lakh on 12 lakh is a 10 per cent rise.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: A rise of 6 percentage points is not a 6 per cent rise; on a base of 60 it is a 10 per cent rise.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The Shivaji Nagar public library had 4,000 members in 2024 and 5,000 in 2025. The number of books borrowed from it rose from 48,000 in 2024 to 55,000 in 2025.

**Conclusions:**
I. The average number of books borrowed per member was lower in 2025 than in 2024.
II. The library added new books to its collection in 2025.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: 48,000 ÷ 4,000 = 12 books per member in 2024 and 55,000 ÷ 5,000 = 11 in 2025.
II does not follow: more borrowing does not show that new books were bought; the collection is not mentioned.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: Total borrowing rose, but members rose faster, so the per-member figure fell.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A member of the Shanti Nagar library may borrow rare books only if he or she has been a member for at least two years. Ritu joined the library 18 months ago.

**Conclusions:**
I. Any member who has been with the library for three years can borrow rare books.
II. Ritu cannot borrow rare books from the library at present.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: "only if" gives a necessary condition; two years' membership does not by itself guarantee permission.
II follows: Ritu has been a member for 18 months, less than two years, so she does not meet the necessary condition.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Reading "only if" as "if" makes I look right; it is the converse error.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Rakesh and Vinod are the only candidates for the post of treasurer of a residents' association. The candidate with more votes wins; if both get the same number of votes, the post goes to the older candidate. Rakesh is older than Vinod, and the votes are now being counted.

**Conclusions:**
I. Rakesh will become the treasurer.
II. Vinod will become the treasurer.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither follows on its own: Rakesh wins if he gets more votes or ties, Vinod wins if he gets more votes, and the count is not over.
Every possible result gives the post to exactly one of the two, so I and II are complementary: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: The tie rule favours Rakesh, but it does not make him certain to win — Vinod may simply get more votes.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** In a city, 40 per cent of the residents who own a car also own a two-wheeler.

**Conclusions:**
I. 40 per cent of the city's two-wheeler owners also own a car.
II. 60 per cent of the city's residents do not own a two-wheeler.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the 40 per cent is of car owners; as a share of two-wheeler owners the same group could be any size, depending on how many own two-wheelers.
II does not follow: the remaining 60 per cent are car owners without a two-wheeler, not 60 per cent of all residents.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: A percentage is tied to its base; changing the base (to two-wheeler owners or to all residents) changes the figure.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A bank's mobile app sends the account holder an alert for every transaction above ₹5,000 in the account. The app sent no alert for a transaction Mr Iyer made from his account with the bank on Monday. On Tuesday, Mrs Iyer made a transaction of ₹8,000 from her own account with the same bank.

**Conclusions:**
I. Mr Iyer's transaction on Monday was of ₹5,000 or less.
II. The app sent Mrs Iyer an alert for her ₹8,000 transaction.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: had Monday's transaction been above ₹5,000, the app would have sent an alert; it sent none, so the amount was ₹5,000 or less.
II follows: ₹8,000 is above ₹5,000, so the rule requires an alert.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: I uses the contrapositive (no alert → not above ₹5,000), which is valid.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Every private vehicle entering the old city between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. must pay a congestion fee of ₹100, except two-wheelers and vehicles owned by residents of the old city.

**Conclusions:**
I. A private car owned by someone who does not live in the old city must pay ₹100 if it enters the old city at 10 a.m.
II. A two-wheeler owned by someone who lives outside the old city must pay ₹100 if it enters the old city at noon.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the car is a private vehicle, it is not a two-wheeler, its owner is not a resident, and 10 a.m. is within the charging hours.
II does not follow: two-wheelers are exempt whoever owns them.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: Check every exemption before applying the main rule; the owner's address does not matter for two-wheelers.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Of the 300 farmers in Kheda village who applied for crop insurance this year, 240 received claim payments after the hailstorm in March.

**Conclusions:**
I. 80 per cent of the farmers in Kheda village received crop-insurance payments after the hailstorm.
II. 60 of the farmers in Kheda village who applied for crop insurance this year did not receive claim payments after the March hailstorm.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: 240 is 80 per cent of the 300 applicants, not of all the farmers in the village, whose number is not given.
II follows: 300 − 240 = 60 applicants did not receive payments.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Watch the base: "farmers who applied" is a smaller group than "farmers in the village".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The sale deed for Mr Bansal's plot will be registered on Monday if the buyer's bank loan is sanctioned by Friday; if the loan is not sanctioned by Friday, the sale will be called off.

**Conclusions:**
I. The sale deed for Mr Bansal's plot will be registered on Monday.
II. The sale of Mr Bansal's plot will be called off.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither follows on its own: whether the loan will be sanctioned by Friday is not known.
The loan either is or is not sanctioned by Friday, and the statement fixes one outcome for each case, so exactly one of I and II will happen: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: Two "if" branches that cover both possibilities make the outcomes complementary.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** From 1 November, the state government will give a subsidy of ₹20,000 to every farmer who installs a solar water pump.

**Conclusions:**
I. More farmers in the state will install solar water pumps after 1 November than before.
II. Farmers who installed solar water pumps in September will also get the subsidy.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the subsidy may encourage farmers, but how many will install pumps is a prediction.
II does not follow: the scheme starts on 1 November; nothing says it covers pumps installed earlier.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: A scheme that starts on a date is not, unless stated, backdated.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A depositor can close a fixed deposit before maturity only if he or she pays a penalty of 1 per cent of the deposit. Vandana closed her fixed deposit before maturity.

**Conclusions:**
I. Vandana paid a penalty of 1 per cent of her deposit.
II. A depositor who has not paid this penalty has not closed a fixed deposit before maturity.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: "Only if" makes paying the penalty a necessary condition for early closure.
I follows: Vandana closed early, so the necessary condition must have been met. II follows: without the penalty, early closure is not possible.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: "Only if" works backwards: from the result (early closure) you may infer the condition (penalty), not the other way round.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Of the 2,500 complaints received by the electricity board's helpline last month, 60 per cent were about billing and 25 per cent were about power cuts; the rest were about other matters.

**Conclusions:**
I. The helpline received 375 complaints about matters other than billing and power cuts last month.
II. Billing errors are the biggest problem faced by the board's consumers.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: the rest are 100 − 60 − 25 = 15 per cent, and 15 per cent of 2,500 = 375.
II does not follow: complaints to a helpline do not measure all the problems consumers face, and a billing complaint need not be about an error.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: Complaint counts measure what people reported, not the size of each problem.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The 20 employees of a small firm earn an average monthly salary of ₹30,000. The owner, who is not one of the 20 employees, draws a salary of ₹1,00,000 a month.

**Conclusions:**
I. Every employee of the firm earns ₹30,000 a month.
II. The average monthly salary of all 21 people, including the owner, is ₹33,333 when rounded to the nearest rupee.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: an average of ₹30,000 allows salaries above and below it.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: Do not add the owner's salary to the average directly; rebuild the total first.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Kiran and Lalit between them own all 100 shares of a private company, and neither of them owns exactly 50 shares.

**Conclusions:**
I. Kiran owns more than half of the company's shares.
II. Lalit owns more than half of the company's shares.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither follows on its own: we do not know how the 100 shares are split.
Since the two own all 100 shares and the split is not 50–50, one of them must own more than 50 and the other fewer: exactly one of I and II is true, so either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: The pair looks unrelated, but "all 100 shares" plus "not exactly 50" makes it complementary.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** In the six months after the city police started issuing e-challans through traffic cameras, the number of traffic violations recorded was 30 per cent higher than in the previous six months.

**Conclusions:**
I. E-challans have made motorists in the city more careless.
II. Motorists in the city committed more traffic violations in these six months than in the previous six months.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the statement gives no reason for the rise, and nothing links e-challans to motorists' behaviour.
II does not follow: the figure is of violations recorded; cameras may simply be catching violations that were missed before.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: "Recorded" is not "committed" — a change in detection can change the count.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A shop sold a table fan for ₹2,160 after giving two successive discounts of 20 per cent and 10 per cent on its marked price.

**Conclusions:**
I. The marked price of the fan was ₹3,000.
II. The total discount was less than 30 per cent of the marked price.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Selling price = marked price × 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72 × marked price, so marked price = ₹2,160 ÷ 0.72 = ₹3,000. I follows.
Total discount = ₹3,000 − ₹2,160 = ₹840, i.e. 28 per cent of the marked price. II follows.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Successive discounts of 20% and 10% are 28% in all, not 30%.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** Every ATM at Pune railway station accepts cash deposits. No ATM of Sahyadri Bank accepts cash deposits.

**Conclusions:**
I. No ATM of Sahyadri Bank is at Pune railway station.
II. Every ATM that accepts cash deposits is at Pune railway station.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: an ATM at the station must accept deposits, and no Sahyadri Bank ATM does, so none of them can be at the station.
II does not follow: it reverses the first sentence; ATMs elsewhere may also accept deposits.
Answer: Only I follows.
solution.trap: "Every A is B" does not give "every B is A".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The central bank has allowed banks to pay depositors aged 80 and above a higher interest rate than they pay other senior citizens.

**Conclusions:**
I. Every bank will now pay its depositors aged 80 and above a higher interest rate than its other senior-citizen depositors.
II. A bank may now pay its depositors aged 80 and above a higher interest rate than it pays other senior citizens.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: the central bank has given permission, not an order; each bank may or may not use it.
II follows: "allowed" means banks may now do this.
Answer: Only II follows.
solution.trap: "Allowed to" is permission, not obligation.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The audit of a cooperative bank's accounts for 2025–26 has been completed. The audit report, which will state whether any irregularity was found, will be released next month.

**Conclusions:**
I. The audit found irregularities in the bank's accounts for 2025–26.
II. The audit found no irregularity in the bank's accounts for 2025–26.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: Neither follows on its own: the report has not been released.
But the audit is complete, so it either found some irregularity or found none. I and II are exact opposites about the same audit: either I or II follows.
Answer: Either I or II follows.
solution.trap: "Not yet released" means not yet known, not "neither happened".

items.prompt:
**Statement:** A survey of 1,000 bank customers in Kerala found that 72 per cent of them used UPI at least once a week in 2025, against 45 per cent in a similar survey in 2023.

**Conclusions:**
I. Bank customers in Kerala used less cash in 2025 than in 2023.
II. More than 70 per cent of people in India use UPI at least once a week.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I does not follow: more UPI use does not by itself mean less cash use; cash is not measured in the survey.
II does not follow: the survey covers bank customers in Kerala, not people across India.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows.
solution.trap: One rise does not prove a matching fall elsewhere, and one state's sample is not the country.

items.prompt:
**Statement:** The railway has announced that from 1 July the Pune–Nagpur Express, which at present runs three days a week, will run daily.

**Conclusions:**
I. At present, the Pune–Nagpur Express does not run on four days of the week.
II. From 1 July, the Pune–Nagpur Express will run on more days a week than it does now.

Taking the statement to be true, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from it.

steps: I follows: running on three days a week means it does not run on the other 7 − 3 = 4 days.
II follows: daily is seven days a week, more than three.
Answer: Both I and II follow.
solution.trap: Here the present schedule is stated outright ("at present runs three days a week"), so I is not a guess.
